title: Count unordered pairs without running a quadratic loop
prompt: Return how many pairs of distinct positions exist in n items when order does not matter. Valid n is 0..1000000; reject larger n with std::invalid_argument. Return std::uint64_t. Do not enumerate pairs; tests check behavior, so also inspect complexity.
driver: int main(){std::uint64_t n;if(!(std::cin>>n))return 2;try{std::cout<<pairCount(n)<<"\n";}catch(const std::invalid_argument&){std::cout<<"too many items\n";}}

explanation: A nested loop with j=i+1 counts the same pairs but does quadratic work. The formula does fixed arithmetic.
